title: Trains to Swansea
from: the main stations in Wales and England
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Wales Airshow. Swansea station is right in the city centre, about a 20 to 25 minute walk from the seafront. GWR runs a direct train from London Paddington most hours, through Reading, Swindon, Bristol Parkway, Newport and Cardiff, and Transport for Wales brings you in from West Wales, the Marches line from Manchester, Chester and Shrewsbury, and the Heart of Wales line. I’ve added the main connections from Bristol, Birmingham, Gloucester, Southampton and Exeter too. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.

ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the Wales Airshow. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From the station it’s about 20 to 25 minutes on foot. Head down through the city centre to Oystermouth Road and the promenade by the Civic Centre. Oystermouth Road and Mumbles Road are closed on show days, so it’s an easy walk once you’re through town, and you can just follow the crowd.
walkBack: Allow about 25 minutes to walk back up to the station from the seafront, and a fair bit longer when everyone leaves at once.
tip: Trains back to London, Cardiff and Bristol get very busy straight after the flying. I would either leave a little early, or stay in town for something to eat and catch a later train.
If you’re staying for Afterburn on the Saturday evening, look at the last train home before it starts. From the further away stations the last good connection can leave Swansea before the fireworks.
There were engineering works on the airshow weekend in 2026, with fewer GWR trains from London. The summer 2027 times come out nearer the show, so please check before you travel.

alt: When I last checked, an anytime day return from Cardiff was £15.30 and from Llanelli £7.60, so the local trains are cheap.

From London, Reading or Bristol I would book an advance ticket early, as it can save a lot. If you’re going as a family, a Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, so it may well pay for itself on this one trip.
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows journeys from twenty main stations, with the changes that work well. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 2 November 2026. These are this winter’s weekend times, and the summer 2027 times will follow, so please check before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway where it could be traced, and station to station on a few short stretches, so treat it as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: Every main line into Swansea. Most trains into Swansea are run by Transport for Wales and GWR, with CrossCountry, South Western Railway, West Midlands Railway and Avanti West Coast on some of the connections. I’ve only included journeys where the whole trip works on a weekend with sensible changes. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there.

pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, especially from London and England, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. They can sell out on a big weekend, so I would book as soon as the summer times are out.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you don’t know when you’ll want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.

A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, and it can pay for itself in one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Which station is closest to the show?

Swansea. It’s right in the city centre, about a 20 to 25 minute walk down to the seafront by the Civic Centre. Oystermouth Road and Mumbles Road are closed on show days, so it’s an easy walk once you’re through town.
Do I need a ticket for the show?

No. Watching from the seafront is free, so it’s only the train fare to think about. The Flight Deck seating, the Sky Lounge and the evening seats were paid extras in 2026, booked through the official website.
The 2027 date hasn’t been announced yet. In 2026 it was Saturday 25 and Sunday 26 July, so I have used weekend times here until the 2027 details are out.
Will there be extra trains on show days?
When I last checked, nothing had been announced for 2027. Engineering works on the line from London have hit the airshow weekend before, so please check nearer the time.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
Can I get a bus from the station?

In 2026 buses across Swansea were free every Saturday and Sunday through the summer, with late services for the Saturday night show. I would check if the offer runs again in 2027, as it may save your legs after a long day.
access: Trains can work really well for an airshow, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
Check the station has step free access to every platform you need, both ways.
In 2025 there were accessible viewing areas at the Cenotaph and the civic site, so I would check the official accessibility page for 2027.
